transcript: Like waitress and bridges of Madison County before it, a new adultery musical has entered the musical theatre canon. The show is called A walk on the moon, based on the movie of the same name, which just began performances off Broadway. I was invited to an early preview, and now I get to tell you what to expect. Like I said, this is a show about adultery, and I do think that your personal enjoyment will depend on how you feel about adultery being depicted in musicals, because cheating is obviously a topic that a lot of people have really strong feelings on. And it can admittedly be really tough to watch your protagonist commit these acts, especially when it's being done in such a self destructive manner, because in this case, the husband is, by all accounts, a really great guy. This is not one of those shows where you are rooting for the affair or for her to get out of a bad relationship. In fact, her attraction to her affair partner seems to be more about what he represents rather than the man himself, which is this new age hippie lifestyle that she feels like she never got to experience herself, having gotten pregnant and married at a very young age. The show takes place in the summer of 1969, which is known as the summer of love. It's when the hippie movement was kind of at its peak. Woodstock took place that summer. It's also The summer where we landed on the moon. Both of which do factor into the plot here. But I don't wanna give too much more away. But overall I thought this musical was pretty solid, especially with it being an early preview. It is LED by Talia Sussower, a former Elphaba, so of course she gets a big 11:00 number where she gets to belt her face off. She is also joined by her parade co star Max Chernin, Andrea Burns, Sam Gravitte. It's actually a pretty stacked cast, and the music I thought was actually pretty good. It didn't leave much of an impression on first listen, but I did enjoy it as I was watching it. And the show itself is surprisingly funny. I think similar to waitress, it is able to find a lot of these comedic moments amidst the drama. And I did find myself invested in these characters and rooting for the family to stay together. So I'm very curious to see how it continues to evolve over the preview period. But even as is just based on what I saw at third preview, I do think it is a pretty solid addition to the adultery musical canon.
reasoning: Reviewer calls it 'pretty solid,' praises the cast, comedy, and finds himself invested, though notes music didn't leave a strong first impression and flags the adultery theme as a potential barrier for some viewers.
